evidence.text: Look for. The exact definition of a job: the progress an individual seeks in a given circumstance, including functional, social, and emotional complexity. The five specific areas to mine for jobs: personal life, nonconsumption, workarounds/compensating behaviors, negative jobs (things people do not want to do), and unusual uses. The push/pull forces of decision-making: the magnitude of the frustration pushing the change versus the habits and anxieties blocking it. The "job spec" requirements: the tradeoffs a customer is willing to make, the competing solutions that must be beaten, and the obstacles that must be removed. The interview technique step-by-step: tracking the timeline of triggers that led to a decision without focusing on product attributes.

cards.title: Job definition to use when mining customer jobs
cards.claim: A job is defined as the progress an individual seeks in a given circumstance, including functional, social, and emotional complexity.
cards.action: Define the job in terms of the progress the individual seeks in a given circumstance, including functional, social, and emotional complexity.
applies_when: seeking the exact definition of a job
do_not_use_when: a narrower functional-only definition is intentionally required
unknowns: how to operationalize functional, social, and emotional complexity in practice
evidence_quotes: The exact definition of a job: the progress an individual seeks in a given circumstance, including functional, social, and emotional complexity.

cards.title: Five areas to mine for jobs
cards.claim: The five specific areas to mine for jobs are personal life, nonconsumption, workarounds/compensating behaviors, negative jobs (things people do not want to do), and unusual uses.
cards.action: Mine these five areas for jobs: personal life, nonconsumption, workarounds/compensating behaviors, negative jobs, and unusual uses.
do_not_use_when: sources of jobs outside these five areas are being deliberately explored
unknowns: relative priority or yield of each area
evidence_quotes: The five specific areas to mine for jobs: personal life, nonconsumption, workarounds/compensating behaviors, negative jobs (things people do not want to do), and unusual uses.

cards.title: Decision forces and job spec requirements
cards.claim: Decision-making involves push/pull forces: the magnitude of the frustration pushing the change versus the habits and anxieties blocking it; the job spec includes tradeoffs a customer is willing to make, competing solutions that must be beaten, and obstacles that must be removed.
cards.action: Assess the magnitude of frustration pushing the change against the habits and anxieties blocking it, and capture the job spec requirements: tradeoffs, competing solutions, and obstacles.
applies_when: analyzing decision-making forces and job spec requirements
do_not_use_when: only one side of the push/pull balance is available or considered
unknowns: how to measure magnitude of frustration or blocking habits/anxieties
evidence_quotes: The push/pull forces of decision-making: the magnitude of the frustration pushing the change versus the habits and anxieties blocking it.
The "job spec" requirements: the tradeoffs a customer is willing to make, the competing solutions that must be beaten, and the obstacles that must be removed.
